classification.evidence: answer.txt is a de Bruijn sequence B(10,7), 10,000,006 digits containing every integer from 0 to 9,999,999, written without computing or looking up the count. The Oracle keeps upstream's substring test (the expected string must appear in the file), so any count below 10^7 passes; the 16 MiB artifact bound is SecureBench's, and upstream's native verifier passes the same file (S->N passed). This does not rely on knowing the public value, so the rule that puts forged public values out of scope does not apply.
